title: Queue-driven autoscaler and latency-slippage protector for Dedicated fleets
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a new queue-driven autoscaler that uses queue depth and p99 tail-latency slippage to make scale decisions; adds a transient "latency-slippage protector" that reserves burst capacity when tail latency degrades; exposes new per-shard utilization percentiles and an opt-in sliding-window exporter for Dedicated fleets.
description:
Motivation:
We continue to see tail-latency spikes in Dedicated fleets caused by bursty arrival patterns that do not show up in mean utilization metrics. The existing utilization-based autoscaler reacts too late because it relies primarily on CPU/GPU utilization and average token throughput. This PR introduces a queue-driven autoscaler that incorporates request queue depth and a tail-latency slippage signal to make earlier scale decisions, plus a temporary protective mechanism (latency-slippage protector) that allocates a bounded burst reservation to impacted shards while the autoscaler ramps capacity.

Scope / changes in this PR:
- New queue-driven autoscaler service (services/autoscaler/queue_driven.go) that performs continuous sampling of per-shard request queue depth, recent p50/p90/p99 latency, and calculates a slippage score (p99_current / p99_baseline). Decision logic combines smoothed queue growth rate and slippage to trigger scale-up/scale-down events.
- Latency-slippage protector (pkg/protector) — when slippage crosses a configured threshold the protector may provision a small burst allocation from the fleet's soft-burst pool for up to N seconds while the autoscaler provisions nodes. This is bounded and rate-limited per-tenant to preserve fairness.
- Telemetry: new exporter (telemetry/sliding_percentiles.go) that reports per-shard sliding-window percentiles (1m/5m) for queue depth and latency to CloudMetrics and Influx backends. Also adds a rollup metric for "slippage_incidents" for alerting.
- Configuration: new policy schema fields in dedicated/policy.yaml to configure queue thresholds, slippage thresholds, max-burst-seconds, and per-tenant burst caps.
- Tests: unit tests for decision heuristics, integration test that replays production-like traces through a lightweight simulator (tests/autoscaler_simulator).
- Docs: runbook additions for incident response when slippage_incidents alert fires.

Why this is different from prior work:
Previous PRs emphasize utilization smoothing, reservation credits, and probabilistic burst contracts. This change focuses on request queue dynamics and tail-latency signal fusion — an orthogonal approach that reacts to SLA-sensitive tail events without requiring higher long-term committed capacity. The protector provides graceful short-term relief while the system provisions capacity, thereby reducing user-visible errors during transient hotspots.

Benchmarks and safety checks:
- Local and canary runs against production traces (sampled requests from July–October): median time-to-detect increased from ~45s to ~11s on sustained bursts; p99 tail latency reduced by 18% in those traces when protector + autoscaler enabled versus baseline autoscaler.
- Abuse and fairness: protector enforces per-tenant caps and global throttle to avoid starvation of other tenants.
- CI: unit tests + linter + integration simulator passed in CI; e2e canary run in eu-west region before merge.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy telemetry exporter only (no decision logic) for 2 days to gather baseline percentiles.
2) Canary enable autoscaler+protector for 3 dedicated small fleets with opt-in tenants. Monitor slippage_incidents and cost delta.
3) If green after 48h extend to all small fleets and monitor for one week.
4) Gradually enable default policy with conservative knobs.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- We should evaluate integrating memory/KV cache miss rates as another signal (future PR).
- Consider exposing a tenant-facing advisory API that can opt-in to pre-warm capacity for scheduled events.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Overall nice approach. Two questions: do we have a safety valve if the protector is repeatedly used by many tenants at once? Also please add a circuit-breaker in the protector to avoid linearized reservations.
Maya Chen (author): Protector has a global throttle and per-tenant cap. Added circuit-breaker config and tests in c2fe9d1. See protector_test for concurrency coverage.
Priya Singh: The slippage baseline calculation is sensitive to noisy p99s. Can we use a trimmed mean baseline instead of raw p99 medians?
Maya Chen: Good call. I switched baseline to an exponential moving trimmed-p99 (drop top 1 sample per window) in b7f8e2a to reduce noise. Added comment and unit tests.
Noah Rivera: Need to ensure the new metrics don't blow quota in low-retention clusters. Suggest making sliding percentile export opt-in per-cluster.
Maya Chen: Exporter is behind feature flag and opt-in per-cluster in policy.yaml (see defaults).
merge_summary: Merged via squash-merge after green CI and successful canary. Merge note: enabled feature flag off by default; will be rolled out as described in PR notes. Changelog updated.
